A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChA-MAEViT work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on CHAMMI, JUMP-CP and So2Sat, including benchmark comparisons, component analyses and supplementary novel-channel adaptation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds 38-Cloud segmentation results, further component-ablation entries and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The masking algorithm, memory tokens, channel-aware decoder, hybrid fusion and training objectives remain unchanged. Section 3.2 changes the memory-token description from cross-attention to self-attention, consistent with the existing prepended-token transformer formulation. The added explanations do not establish an architectural or procedural replacement.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual segmentation evaluation on 38-Cloud (Table 3), extending the work beyond classification and representation learning to dense prediction. CHAMMI, JUMP-CP, So2Sat and the previously reported missing-channel and novel-channel scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the matched benchmark, SSL and masking comparisons. The new segmentation comparison uses existing ChannelViT, DiChaViT and MAE/CA-MAE combinations; no distinct new baseline procedure is documented. Adding the CA-MAE citation to the existing MAE comparison does not establish a baseline replacement.

E3.justification: The reported CHAMMI learning rate changes from 0.00004 to 0.0004, and the JUMP-CP/So2Sat peak rate changes from 0.0005 to 0.0004 (v1 Section 9; v2 Appendix E). Existing splits, training durations, batch sizes and backbone comparisons remain intact. The added segmentation experiment introduces accuracy, IoU, precision, recall and F1 evaluation. The PDFs do not establish whether the learning-rate revisions reflect reruns.

E4.justification: v2 Table 4 consolidates existing component studies and adds JUMP-CP memory-token and fusion ablation results. Appendix F.1 adds a FLOPs comparison, and the displayed DCP sensitivity sweep is extended. Most other analyses, including model scaling, reconstruction and novel-channel adaptation, already appeared in v1; moving the memory-attention analysis into the main text is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Table 2 gains uncertainty entries alongside previously reported point estimates. The memory-token sensitivity curves and decoder comparison gain shaded bands or error bars in v2 Figures 3 and 5. Three-run mean/standard-deviation reporting already existed in v1; no increase in run counts or new significance-testing procedure is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds segmentation, ablation and FLOPs results. Its new Table 3 reports IoU 0.894±0.002 for ChA-MAEViT versus 0.886±0.004 for DiChaViT+CA-MAE. Existing results also change: Table 1 JUMP-CP Partial becomes 68.05±0.21 instead of 68.15±0.10, and several Table 2 means are revised. The runtime example switches from CHAMMI on one GPU to JUMP-CP on two GPUs, so the reported 5X-to-6X difference is not a same-setting speedup.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of masking, patch projection, reconstruction losses and token fusion are retained. Several equations become inline or are renumbered, without changing their mathematical substance. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs that are subsequently added, removed or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction's contribution statement adds consistent gains on Cloud-38, extending the demonstrated scope to segmentation. The four principal methodological contributions and the abstract/conclusion claim of 3.0–21.5% improvements on the original three benchmarks remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix A discusses difficulties adapting unseen channels under domain shifts and the computational burden of additional hyperparameter tuning. Appendix F.9 explains blurry reconstructions through MSE averaging, the lightweight decoder and the representation-learning objective. v1 already acknowledged the novel-channel performance gap, so these additions expand existing qualifications rather than introduce a new failure experiment.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code availability statement and link, more explicit masking and memory-token defaults, and validation-based checkpoint selection. It also revises learning-rate and runtime disclosures. However, Appendix F.5 duplicates the DCP Alternate discussion with conflicting patch-mask defaults of 0.25 and 0.75, leaving that setting ambiguous.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references concerning cloud segmentation, hyperspectral/multispectral augmentation and reconstruction losses or geospatial MAEs. Appendix C expands the explanation of how DiChaViT combined with MAE relates to CA-MAE. The central positioning against existing MAEs and fixed-ratio channel masking remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative are retained, with localized condensation, terminology corrections and expanded explanations. Dataset/setup headings are compressed, implementation discussion is moved into the appendix, and supplementary sections are reorganized as Appendices A–F. The duplicated paragraph in Appendix F.5 is a new editorial defect.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column formatting to a predominantly single-column NeurIPS layout, substantially rearranging displays. Figure 1 becomes side-by-side, the memory-token and reconstruction-weight plots are merged into Figure 3, and the memory-attention heatmaps are reoriented and moved into the main text. Segmentation and consolidated ablation tables, a FLOPs plot and uncertainty displays are added.

improvement.justification: The added segmentation and component evidence, uncertainty displays and project-code disclosure modestly strengthen validation and transparency. The gains are limited by missing segmentation setup details, unexplained learning-rate revisions and contradictory DCP Alternate defaults in Appendix F.5. The core method and most supporting evidence were already present in v1.
